key_insight: AI on routine echocardiography can spot prominent epicardial adipose tissue and flag residual cardiometabolic risk beyond BMI.
clinical_relevance: This could turn standard heart ultrasound into a low-cost screen for hidden epicardial fat burden linked to adverse metabolic health.
method: Trained the video-based deep learning model PanAdipo on 1.11 million echo videos from 28,797 studies with expert report labels for prominent epicardial adipose tissue.
Validated performance across multiple external cohorts, including TTE, POCUS, MIMIC-IV, and MESA, plus paired cardiac CT angiography.
Compared AI scores with CT-derived epicardial fat measures, BMI, and metabolic biomarkers/disease outcomes.
evidence_signal: PanAdipo achieved AUROC 0.86 for report-labeled prominent EAT on held-out echo data, up to 0.93 with selected views, and 0.91-0.95 for CT-defined high EAT; it correlated more strongly with indexed EAT volume (rho=0.76) than BMI (rho=0.41).
watch_item: Because the model was trained and validated in retrospective datasets, real-world deployment still needs prospective testing, workflow integration, and attention to site-specific imaging quality.
paper_title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies Prominent Epicardial Adipose Tissue Associated With an Adverse Cardiometabolic Profile
